BioNova Pharmaceuticals - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the BioNova Pharmaceuticals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone and wait for further instructions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss BioNova Pharmaceuticals' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Lisa Wong, Chief Scientific Officer; Karen Lee, Head of Commercial.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO of BioNova Pharmaceuticals.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. BioNova delivered a strong performance in the second quarter, driven by robust demand for our innovative oncology and rare disease portfolio, including standout contributions from our new antibody-drug conjugate NovaLink-301 and our gene therapy GeneFix. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, with particular excitement around our business development momentum, clinical advancements, and operational efficiencies that are positioning us for sustained growth.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, with a focus on navigating the pricing and reimbursement landscape, accelerating new product launches and market share gains, advancing business development through licensing deals, acquisitions, and partnerships, improving gross margin trends via manufacturing efficiencies, enhancing marketing and sales effectiveness, and strengthening our cash flow and balance sheet. We are particularly excited about NovaLink-301 and its potential to capture meaningful share in the HER2-low breast cancer market while driving margin expansion across our portfolio.

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a solid second quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $1.78 billion, an increase of 25% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong uptake of our new launches like NovaLink-301 and GeneFix, alongside growth in our established oncology assets such as OncoTarget-1, our PD-1 inhibitor, and LymphoCure, our CAR-T therapy.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $350 million, or $2.10 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $420 million, or $2.50 per share.

Our operating expenses were $900 million, reflecting continued investments in R&D to support our pipeline, offset by efficiencies in SG&A. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to fuel our pipeline advancements. Our cash position remains strong at $2.5 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenue of $7.5 to $8.0 billion, adjusted EPS of $10.00 to $11.00, reflecting raised expectations for new product contributions and business development inflows.

Let me now dive deeper into several key aspects shaping our results. First, on the pricing and reimbursement landscape, which remains a dynamic driver of our financial performance. Our portfolio, including flagship OncoTarget-1, LymphoCure, and GeneFix for rare genetic disorders, operates under intense scrutiny. In the U.S., representing 68% of our Q2 net product revenues at $1.2 billion, list prices held steady year-over-year—OncoTarget-1 at $185,000 per patient-year, comparable to peers like Keytruda. Net realized prices, however, reflect a gross-to-net adjustment of 48% in Q2, up 300 basis points year-over-year, largely from elevated rebates to pharmacy benefit managers such as Express Scripts and CVS Caremark. For OncoTarget-1, rebates averaged 52% of gross sales due to portfolio carve-outs and utilization management in high-cost oncology combinations, but we recouped 15% via value-based contracts linked to overall response rates and progression-free survival, echoing Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo arrangements.

The Inflation Reduction Act's maximum fair price negotiations pose challenges, with OncoTarget-1 targeted for the 2026 tranche after $1.8 billion in Medicare Part D spend last year; we're modeling a 25-35% reduction in net average selling prices, similar to projections for other high-spend drugs. Countermeasures include expanding our 340B strategy—Q2 discounts reached 42% of eligible sales, up from 38%, with a 20% growth in our contract pharmacy network targeting rural hospitals. Patient assistance covered 12,000 patients, averting $150 million in bad debt. Average selling price reporting supported gains, with OncoTarget-1 up 2% sequentially to $142,000 on earlier-line adoption post-Phase III ELEVATE data, while LymphoCure held at $420,000 despite CMS site-neutral reforms, securing add-on payments for 85% of our 120 U.S. treatment centers.

Ex-U.S., contributing 32% or $580 million, shows divergence. In Europe, EMA label expansions for OncoTarget-1 enabled premium pricing at an average annual treatment cost of €162,000 in Germany per IQWiG's assessment, a 12% uplift over comparators; France negotiated GeneFix to €1.9 million per dose, competitive with Zolgensma. The UK's NICE approved LymphoCure via the Innovative Medicines Fund, achieving 65% eligible patient uptake, though with outcome-based clawbacks if survival data trails our 28-month forecast. Asia-Pacific shines: Japan's PMDA set GeneFix at ¥450 million with 90% national health insurance coverage, and China's Sinopharm partnership listed OncoTarget-1 on the NRDL at a 32% U.S. discount, fueling 45% volume growth against biosimilar pressures akin to Herceptin, where Roche biosimilars took 28% share.

Globally, biosimilars advanced to 22% penetration for reference monoclonal antibodies, eroding $80 million in legacy revenues, but novel modalities like GeneFix retain 95% pricing power. Value-based deals now span 35% of ex-U.S. sales, up from 22%, benchmarked to real-world progression-free survival from Flatiron and IQVIA. Our strategy rests on real-world evidence from 500,000 patient records, reversing 15% of negative health technology assessments like Italy's for LymphoCure; portfolio risk-sharing for 20% of 2025 launches; and $25 million in Inflation Reduction Act advocacy with PhRMA peers, plus AI rebate forecasting at 98% accuracy. We guide full-year U.S. gross-to-net at 46-50%, ex-U.S. pricing flat to 3% up, confident in 12% net price growth excluding erosion, backed by our cash reserves for gene editing tuck-ins.

Building on this, our new product launches and market share gains are delivering exceptional momentum. NovaLink-301, our HER2-low metastatic breast cancer ADC launched U.S. late Q4 2023 post-Phase 3 NOVA-HER2 accelerated approval, posted Q2 net sales of $285 million—47% quarter-over-quarter growth, surpassing $240 million consensus, with year-to-date over $650 million and full-year guidance raised to $1.2 billion from $1.1 billion. IQVIA shows 18% U.S. share by June-end, from 6% at launch, eroding Enhertu (45% share) and Trodelvy (22%), thanks to 25% lower interstitial lung disease at 2.1% and superior tumor penetration. U.S. drove 92% of sales with new-to-brand prescriptions up 32% to 28,000; Europe added $22 million post-EMA approval; Asia-Pacific royalties from Takeda hit $8 million. We've scaled Singapore manufacturing to 150,000 vials monthly and expanded our sales force to 450 oncology reps, shifting 15% share from T-DM1.

GeneFix, our AAV gene therapy for SMA Type 1 launched ex-U.S. Q1 2024 post-FDA approval, reached $112 million globally, 20% above guidance, with peak potential at $2.5 billion by 2028. Global share is 14%, challenging Zolgensma via 20% lower dose and 18-month shelf-life. U.S. sales $85 million with 95% payer coverage; Europe $20 million on NICE and AIFA nods. New products drove 42% of Q2 revenue, up from 28% year-over-year, expanding gross margins 15 points to 82%. Forward risks like payer scrutiny on $18,500 vial pricing are met with $500 million in Phase 4 real-world evidence and digital partnerships, alongside next-gen assets like TROP2-ADC and CRISPR CAR-T.

Shifting to business development, we've executed transformative deals generating $450 million upfront in Q2, with $2.5 billion milestones and 12-18% royalties; year-to-date $1.1 billion, up 35%. Key was the global license of our next-gen ADC BGN-ADC-217 to Merck for $250 million upfront plus $1.2 billion milestones, royalties 14-18%, leveraging Keytruda combos in Phase 2 basket trials. Regional PROTAC license to Roche for fibrosis yielded $120 million upfront, $800 million milestones. We acquired Aura Biotech for $550 million, adding CRISPR LNP for extrahepatic editing in DMD and alpha-1 deficiency. Expanded Pfizer partnership on obesity bispecific covers 60% Phase 3 costs for ex-U.S. rights. These fund 40% of R&D, with a $500 million funnel ahead.

On gross margin trends and manufacturing efficiency, we achieved GAAP gross margin of 78.2%, up 170 basis points sequentially and 320 year-over-year; non-GAAP 79.5%. Product mix led with BPI-Lirix-like GLP-1 at 42% revenue and 85% margins, offsetting JAK margins. COGS at 21.8% of revenue benefited from locked API contracts and 88% utilization. Our $450 million NextGen program delivered continuous manufacturing yields of 12-15 g/L for mAbs, AI predictive analytics cutting defects to 0.8%, and Singapore hub at 95% utilization. U.S. at 82%, Europe 85%, Asia leading. Headwinds like pricing shaved 40 basis points, countered by biosimilar pipeline. Guide Q4 78.5-80.0%, full-year 77.8%.

Marketing and sales effectiveness metrics show TRx for NovaRheum at 1.47 million, up 12% QoQ/28% YoY, NRx 342,000 with 32.4% share of initiations; OncoVantage TRx 856,000, NRx share 26.8%. Reps averaged 8.7 calls weekly at 92% compliance, close rate 27.2%. U.S. 78% TRx, Europe accelerating, emerging doubling. Omnichannel ROI at $142/TRx, digital 42% interactions. Guide NovaRheum $2.8-3.0 billion, OncoVantage $1.6-1.8 billion.

Finally, cash flow and balance sheet highlights: $3.4 billion liquidity, up 12% QoQ, runway over 4.5 years. Net debt 0.8x EBITDA post-3.75% refi saving $25 million interest. Operating cash $720 million, 105% conversion; investing $410 million; financing $120 million; free cash $310 million. Guide FY24 operating cash $2.6-2.8 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Raj Patel, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Michael. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, topline data from the Phase 3 NOVA-SMA2 trial for GeneFix label expansion in SMA Type 2 is on track for H1 2025, while NovaLink-301's Phase 4 real-world study confirms tolerability advantages. LymphoCure add-on payments expanded to more centers. We expect key milestones like Phase 2 readouts for our TROP2-ADC and bispecifics in Q4.

Next, Dr. Lisa Wong will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Lisa Wong, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Raj. We are making significant strides in early-stage research. Aura integration bolsters CRISPR editing for DMD, with preclinical POC in cardiomyocytes at 40% efficiency. PROTAC platform advances fibrosis degrader post-Roche deal, and AAV capsid library enhancements cut costs 25%. We're advancing three next-gen assets toward 2025 INDs in immuno-oncology and gene editing.

Now I'll turn the call over to Karen Lee, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Karen Lee, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Lisa. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with new products at 42% of revenue. NovaLink-301 captured 18% U.S. share via 450 reps and KOL activations; GeneFix hit 14% global SMA share on payer wins. Marketing campaigns proved effective, with omnichannel yielding 3.2x engagement lift, DTC driving 2.1 million uniques, and precision targeting boosting prescribers 68%. NRx growth positions us strongly amid biosimilars.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Elena.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you, Karen. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for queuing questions. Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the pricing side, with IRA negotiations looming for OncoTarget-1, can you elaborate on your 340B expansion and value-based contracting progress?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thanks, Jane. Michael?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Absolutely, Jane. Our 340B discounts hit 42% of eligible sales, with 20% network growth into rural areas, and value-based deals recouped 15% on ORR/PFS for OncoTarget-1. RWE has flipped HTAs, and we're piloting risk-sharing for 20% of launches.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. On new launches, how sustainable is NovaLink-301's share gains versus Enhertu, and any supply updates?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Thanks, Tom. Sustainability comes from 25% lower ILD and deeper penetration; we've scaled to 150,000 vials/month in Singapore, with 32% NBRx growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks. For business development, details on the Aura acquisition synergies and milestone risks?

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Hi Lisa. Aura's LNP enhances extrahepatic editing, cutting costs 25% and adding DMD/alpha-1 assets; historical milestone hit rate is 75%, de-risked by RMAT designations.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Patel with Citi. Please go ahead.

Mark Patel, Citi:
Thanks. On gross margins, what's driving the efficiency gains, and FY outlook?

Karen Lee, Head of Commercial:
Mark, continuous manufacturing hit 12-15 g/L yields, AI cut defects to 0.8%, Singapore at 95% utilization. Full-year guide 77.8%, with 200-300 bps expansion ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Wong, Barclays:
Quick one on marketing metrics—NRx conversion trends and biosimilar impact?

Karen Lee, Head of Commercial:
Emily, 87% NRx to 90-day fills, close rate 27.2%; SC formulation and expansions counter TNF biosimilars for 20-25% FY25 NRx growth.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the BioNova Pharmaceuticals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
